statement: First-time customers do not place a second order because substitutions surprise them at the door.
falsifier: If most interviewees describe no substitution problem, or say a swap would not stop them reordering, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 5 of 12 describe a recent substitution they only found out about at delivery and say it put them off ordering again.

statement: Asking customers to approve substitutions by push notification before the driver leaves will raise second orders.
falsifier: If interviewees who had a surprise swap say they could not or would not answer a notification in time, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 4 of 12 describe a moment when they would have answered a swap request in time.

statement: Two-hour delivery windows do not fit working households' days.
falsifier: If most working interviewees picked a window without trouble on their last order, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 4 of 12 describe rearranging their day, or missing a delivery, because of the window.

statement: A shared household list that anyone at home can add to will raise basket size and repeat orders.
falsifier: If interviewees say one person keeps the whole list and nobody else adds to it, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 3 of 12 describe someone else in the household adding items before an order.

statement: Households will pay 9.99 a month for a delivery pass with free delivery on every order.
falsifier: If most interviewees name a price below 5 a month, or say they order too rarely for a pass, this hypothesis is false.
criterion: We are right if at least 5 of 12 name 9.99 a month or more for a pass before being offered that number.
